terms.text: a longest consecutive sequence of lines where each line has text after strip(), tracked by opening index a when a non-blank line starts and closing when a blank line or the end of range is reached
a directed graph built from calls where each node is an SCC root from comp and each edge connects two roots that belong to different SCCs, used by height() to compute layer numbers
the single dict with keys layer, text, takes, gives, lines, and optionally children that compile_block() returns after one_pass() collapses all cells
the string ctx built from done[] entries for each function bl calls, listing each callee's short name, takes, gives, and text, prepended to the PROMPT so the model knows what compiled callees do

the name v stored in comp[w] for every w in a strongly connected component, assigned when low[v] == idx[v] in strong(), used as the node identity in the condensed DAG

emit(node):
kids = kids_of(node) — direct statement children of node

if not kids: spans.append([node.lineno, node.end_lineno])
return — leaf node gets its own span

a = None — start of current non-blank run
for n in node's line range:
    own = n not in covered and line n is non-blank
    if own and a is None: a = n — open a non-blank run

map.name: check_pass
map.takes: model reply m, cells list, stmts, blank line set, ess line set, bad function name set
map.gives: validated groups list
map.text: check_pass(m, cells, stmts, blank, ess, bad) -> groups — asserts that groups cover all cells in order, each group is contiguous and non-empty, no group names a function not called by this block, no first-pass group exceeds 15 non-blank lines, and no group cuts a statement across its boundary

children.text: def check_pass(m, cells, stmts, blank, ess, bad):

groups = m.get("groups")
assert groups is a non-empty list
assert len(groups) < len(cells) or len(cells) == 1 — the group count must go down
at = 1 — the next expected cell index

for g in groups:
  a, b = g["cells"]
  assert a == at — each group must start where the last ended
  assert a <= b <= len(cells) — end is in range
  assert g["text"] is a non-empty string
  for w in function names in g["text"]: assert w not in bad — no call this block does not make

got = all line numbers covered by cells a..b, minus blank lines
if b > a and no cell has a text: assert len(got) <= 15 — first-pass group too large
got &= ess
assert at == len(cells) + 1 — the last group must end at the last cell
return groups

map.name: carve
map.takes: line range [a, b], minus spans to exclude, and lines list
map.gives: list of [start, end] spans free of minus and blank lines
map.text: carve(a, b, minus, lines) -> out — returns the free sub-ranges of [a, b] after removing minus spans and trimming blank lines from each end

children.text:
used = all line numbers covered by minus spans
spans = []
run = None — tracks the start of the current free run

for i in range(a, b+2): build spans from free positions
free = i is within [a,b] and not in used
if free and run is None: run = i
if not free and run is not None: spans.append([run, i-1]); run = None

out = []
for s, e in spans: trim leading and trailing blank lines
if s <= e: out.append([s, e])
return out

nodes = nodes_of(tree)
texts = each node's id and text joined by newlines — the text the TERMS prompt sees
low = each node's text lowercased
base = TERMS prompt filled with name, code, texts

note = ""
errs = []

for attempt in range(8): m = ask(base + note)

seen = set()
out = []

for t in terms:
  w = t["term"] — assert non-empty, not duplicate, present in low
  assert t["text"] is a non-empty string
  d = t["defs"] — assert non-empty list with each range inside lines

map.gives: one compiled root node with text, takes, gives, and lines
map.text: compile_block(bl, cells, name, code, lines, stmts, blank, ess, ctx, bad) -> node — drives one_pass() in a loop until the cells collapse to one signed node

children.text:
compile_block(bl, cells, name, code, lines, stmts, blank, ess, ctx, bad)
bstmts = the statements whose line spans fall inside bl["lines"]

stext = ""
if bstmts: stext = the statement ranges formatted as an indented tree — the prompt section the model uses to avoid cut statements

label = bl["name"] last segment + "()" if bl has a node, else "the top-level script code"
span = bl["lines"] ranges joined as a string
layer = 0

while cells has more than one entry or cells[0] has no "takes":
  layer += 1
  final = true when every cell already has a "text"
  cells = one_pass(cells, name, code, lines, stext, bstmts, blank, ess, layer, label, span, ctx, bad, final)
  print bl["name"] pass layer: n -> len(cells)
return cells[0]

map.name: main
map.takes: a source file path from the command line
map.gives: map.json next to the source file
map.text:
main(path) -> map.json — parses, compiles, and writes one map for the whole file
example: {"file": "x.py", "links": […], "terms": […], "map": [{"id": "F01", "text": …, "children": […]}]}

children.text:
path = the file path from sys.argv[1]
src = the text read from path
lines = src split into lines
assert any line is non-blank
code = the lines, each with its number in front — the file the model sees

cells = cells_of(path, src, lines)
stmts = statements(path, src)

blank = the set of blank line numbers
ess = the set of lines in innermost statements — lines the model must not cut across
ess -= blank

blocks = blocks_of(path, src, lines)
body = the top-level AST nodes of src
names = the set of defined function and class names
calls = calls_of(b, body, names) for each block b
lay = layers_of(blocks, calls)

parts = cells grouped by block
for each cell: parts[the block whose line spans hold all its lines] += cell

done = {}
for bl in blocks sorted by (layer, first line):
  ctx = the compiled summaries of the functions bl calls — the context prompt for compile_block()
  if ctx: prefix ctx with the header line
  bad = the function names in names that bl does not call
  root = compile_block(bl, parts[bl["name"]], path.name, code, lines, stmts, blank, ess, ctx, bad)
  root["name"], root["layer"], root["calls"], root["lines"] = the block metadata
  done[bl["name"]] = root

tree = done values sorted by first line
number(tree)
owner = owner_of(tree)
m = {"file": path.name, "links": links(path, owner), "terms": terms_of(path.name, code, lines, tree), "map": tree}
out = map.json next to the source file
write_map(out, m)
print(block count, nodes_of(tree) count, link count, term count, and out path)
